title: What Will It Cost

source.title: ROBERT L MAGINNIS: Iran War cost Republicans Congress. What will it cost America?
source.byline: Robert Maginnis (retired U.S. Army infantry officer; senior fellow for National Security, Family Research Council)
source.note: published 11-08 (date only on the page; the feed stamp 10:00 EST); the 11-08 sweep matched it on 'iran' alone — 'cost of the war' and 'voter poll' are keys on the local terms.json the Action has never read. Read in full on 11-09 via the cloud fetch (the .print page, complete, 31 body paragraphs) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. An opinion page: one voice beside the hed, with the office and the holder each carried once in paraphrase. Cut 11-09 from the 11-08 sweep as the Fox row on the live object that could be read in full — the newer row ('Trump holds all the cards', 10:13 EST) returned a server error on .print and truncated at ¶3 on the main page, so it stays in the queue; my call

object.label: H1c — the price leg read by the vote, from the RI? corner, five days on: the cost conceded in full and itemized. The vote (the Fox News Voter Poll — over a third of voters called the war crucial to their House vote, about six in ten called attacking Iran the wrong decision; a separate Fox survey — nearly twice as many preferred ending involvement to lower gas prices as favored renewed strikes), the dollars (a Pentagon estimate to Congress: $47.1 billion through 16 October, repairs $5–15 billion more by the WSJ), the opportunity cost (the USS George Washington out of the Pacific) and the forward cost, which is the question in the hed. The pump is on the page once, as the exit voters preferred, polled; the Strait once, as a standing threat (¶19). The vehicle is 2006: Iraq, Rumsfeld, Gates, the surge — the author was in the room

zAxis.pos: the war did not cost the vote — the loss has another cause or another owner

object.gear: fast — the vote (weeks to months); the pump on one line as the preferred exit; the dollars a new register (the bill); the slow gear (dollar, P3) not on any line

transformNote: the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) — is not restated; the holder is on the page once, in paraphrase, conceding that the war 'contributed' and that he would do nothing differently (¶6) — the limiter again ('contributed', after 'a piece of it', 'a little bit short term', 'the gasoline', 'fine'). What the page does to the object is accept it whole and send the bill forward: the cost at the vote is given (two polls, the author's own house's), the cost in dollars is given (the Pentagon's figure), and the question becomes what the next two years cost. Nothing on the page moves the owner abroad — the one line on Israel (¶26) asks how closely US decisions track its preferences, which is the 11-05 'easy target' motion at a quarter strength

split.note: one voice beside the hed. The author's migration: 26 → 20 → 24 → 8 → 10 → 12 → 34 → 38 → 18 → 20 → 46 → 40 → 24 → 36 → 30 — fluid through the record (the polls, the bill, the Strait), up into the oscillation zone whenever the page turns to doctrine, 2006 or Tehran's reading of the vote, back down at the close. lines.quote: 'Iran War cost Republicans Congress. What will it cost America?'
lines.note: THE DOOR — the predicate as the headline, in the author's own house's corner; the forward cost as the question
lines.zWhy: a hed that says the war cost Congress has read the vote as the war's

lines.quote: 2006 was Iraq, this time Iran; both chambers, at least seven seats — Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Iowa; the office blamed 'the war his administration launched eight months ago'
lines.note: THE MECHANISM — the loss → the war, with the analogy as its warrant; the seats counted
lines.zWhy: the war named as the loss's cause by analogy and by the office

lines.quote: US forces badly damaged Iran's military, but military success does not guarantee strategic success 'when public support erodes'
lines.note: the predicate in doctrine form — the vote as the war's missing pillar
lines.zWhy: a war won on the field and lost at the vote is a war that cost the vote

lines.quote: the war was why they lost; losing the Senate 'for six years' not worth it
lines.note: CONSTITUTIVE — the office's post of 11-04 in the author's paraphrase, with a clause the Press has not carried (six years); later sighting, the fifth page; not re-filed

lines.quote: the war 'contributed' to the losses; nothing differently; Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon
lines.note: CONSTITUTIVE — the holder's 11-06 gaggle in paraphrase: the limiter ('contributed') after 'a piece of it', 'a little bit short term', 'fine'; later sighting

lines.quote: three days before Epic Fury (Feb. 28) he warned the facts had to be established; never doubted the military could win, doubted there was a plan after — 'eight months later there still is not'
lines.note: the author's own record — the war dated to its first day; the missing plan as the standing fact
lines.zWhy: a war with no plan after it is the war the vote punished

lines.quote: the Fox News Voter Poll: over a third of voters called the war crucial to their House vote; about six in ten said attacking Iran was the wrong decision
lines.note: THE INSTRUMENT — the vote tracker's third reading on the Press (NBC exit poll, the AP Voter Poll, now Fox's own); the page's floor
lines.zWhy: six in ten against the war on the day of the vote, from the holder's corner

lines.quote: a separate Fox survey: nearly twice as many preferred ending involvement 'to lower gas prices' as favored renewed strikes; Americans 'judged the cost too high'
lines.note: THE PUMP AS THE EXIT — the first line on the Press where the price is the polled reason to end the war; the pump's one appearance on the page
lines.zWhy: voters who would end the war to lower gas prices have priced the war at the pump

lines.quote: the Pentagon's estimate to Congress: $47.1 billion through Oct. 16, base repairs excluded; the WSJ puts repairs at $5 billion to $15 billion; Congress must determine the losses
lines.note: THE BILL — the war's cost in dollars, a register the Press has carried once ('per family', 10-29); the primary is the Pentagon's submission
lines.zWhy: a bill itemized is a cost conceded

lines.quote: the opportunity cost: the Japan-based USS George Washington diverted from the Pacific; China 'the principal strategic competitor'
lines.note: the right domain (the war's cost), the wrong plane (the Pacific) — three paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a cost counted in carriers is a cost, read neither way on the vote

lines.quote: Powell's doctrine — clear objectives, overwhelming force, public support, an exit; 'a president cannot sustain a costly war without public support'
lines.note: THE DOCTRINE — the vote as the pillar neglected; the author's 1974 lieutenancy the warrant
lines.zWhy: public support named as the pillar the vote removed

lines.quote: instead of the short campaign promised, eight months of strikes, ceasefires and talks, no durable settlement; Khamenei killed, the regime survives, the nuclear question unresolved, Tehran 'still threatens shipping' through the Strait
lines.note: THE STRAIT — the record of the war's state; the promise ('short campaign') named as unkept; the gate still contested
lines.zWhy: a war promised short and still open at month eight is the war the vote read

lines.quote: in January: investigate losses, demand Pentagon testimony, 'condition appropriations', challenge the war's authority; the holder keeps broad executive power
lines.note: THE CLOCK CHANGES HANDS — the appropriators' clock, named from the RI corner after the LP corner named 11 December (bp 11-06)
lines.zWhy: a war whose funding the vote put in other hands cost the vote

lines.quote: Qalibaf is celebrating — Americans 'rejected war' — which Washington 'must not encourage'; Beijing and Moscow watching
lines.note: THE MIRROR — Tehran's reading of the vote (aj 11-04, 'NO TO WAR') refused from the holder's corner; the vote's meaning policed abroad; the page's highest line
lines.zWhy: a reading of the vote refused is still the vote read as the war's

lines.quote: 2006: Bush replaced Rumsfeld with Gates, then the surge; the holder may face pressure to replace Hegseth — 'new personnel alone' accomplish little
lines.note: THE VEHICLE — the analogy run to its personnel; who answers for the war
lines.zWhy: a war whose secretary may be replaced for the vote cost the vote

lines.quote: the administration divided (Axios): the office and Witkoff for an agreement; Hegseth and Netanyahu for renewed military action; others for economic pressure
lines.note: the record of the split — three camps named; later sighting of the ticket's split (11-04) in its widest form
lines.zWhy: a house divided over whether to end the war is a house that read the vote

lines.quote: advisers who will challenge him; 'an honest accounting of costs'; how closely US decisions 'track Israel's preferences' — overlapping, 'not identical'; define victory — four options
lines.note: THE ASK — the cost's address touched once (Israel's preferences) and left; the 11-05 'easy target' at a quarter strength
lines.zWhy: a page asking for an accounting has conceded there is a bill

lines.quote: reluctant to resume major attacks during diplomacy — room to reconsider 'before more costs accrue'; another warning from the voters; 'battlefield superiority' is not 'a winning strategy'; a credible plan 'at an acceptable price'
lines.note: THE CLOSE — the bill sent forward; the price named as the plan's condition; four paragraphs folded
lines.zWhy: a plan asked for at an acceptable price is a war whose price the vote refused
